amendments.trades_away: Each of the three loose mask discs becomes 2mm taller (9mm -> 11mm rim band), so the brief's own line describing 9mm as their 'tallest feature' is no longer accurate, and the full three-disc stack grows from 27mm to 33mm. This still clears the 40mm axle's stated 18mm bore-engagement depth with axle exposure above the top disc dropping from 22mm to 16mm — still comfortably uncapped, no retaining feature needed, no bed-fit issue (well under the 251mm z limit). The tradeoff is purely cosmetic/proportional: the discs read as slightly thicker in hand and in the hero render than idea.json originally implied.
amendments.why: Two independent repair rounds (board-game-builder, repair mode) confirmed the underside relief the gate demands (a resting tile's 9mm knob standing proud of the well ledge) exactly equals mask_disc_a's ENTIRE stated height budget at the radius where the window-track annulus must remain solid to mask un-revealed wells. There is zero slack: any cut deep enough to clear the knob removes 100% of the disc's material at that radius, severing the ring that connects the disc's bore/hub to its outer rim and destroying the masking mechanic. Round 2 also confirmed the disc's seating height is not a free variable — brief.json's own interfaces 4 and 5 pin the discs flush to the ledge with an exact, load-bearing axle-engagement sum (18mm engaged + 22mm exposed = 40mm stated axle length), so raising the disc off the ledge on a shoulder is not available without also contradicting that stated arithmetic. Raising the disc's own height budget is the only change that opens clearance without touching well_depth, tile_thickness, knob_h, or the seating interfaces — i.e. the smallest-blast-radius fix. +2mm gives a ~1.6-2.0mm remaining wall in the track band after the 9mm-deep relief cut, clearing this pipeline's 1.6mm min_wall_mm.

amendments.trades_away: The obelisk doubles in height (150mm -> 306mm) and can no longer print as a single piece — it now exceeds the 251mm bed z-limit and must be tiled into two printed segments (a lower ~180mm piece and an upper ~126mm cap, exact split left to the builder) joined by a dovetail/spigot seam that keeps the 24mm tile bore continuous through the joint, the same tiling technique this pipeline already uses for any part too big for one bed. On the table this makes reserve_column dramatically taller and narrower-looking than the rest of the set (306mm vs plinth_ring's 70mm and the tallest disc stack's 33mm) — a real change to the object's silhouette and the hero render idea.json implied ('the obelisk's read slot showing the stack still half full' now describes a much taller obelisk than originally pictured), and it becomes the single tallest, most fragile-looking piece in the box even though its 46-70mm cross-section keeps it structurally sound. The full-height read slot (idea.json's stated game-clock feature) is preserved and becomes MORE legible, not less, since it now spans the true full stack.
amendments.why: Two independent repair rounds on the reserve_column gate failure ('reserve_column's 144.0mm usable bore holds only 9 tiles at the true 15.0mm knob-up pitch, short of the 20 setup requires') confirmed this is a genuine, self-acknowledged conflict already flagged in the previous brief's own unstated_in_spec: idea.json states reserve_column is 150mm tall AND that it must hold 20 tiles (30 total minus 10 seeded into wells) AND that tiles stack knob-up — and the tile's own stated geometry (6mm body + 9mm knob, load-bearing, identical across all three families, no complementary socket on the opposing flat face) forces an unavoidable 15mm pitch per tile with no possible nesting. 20 tiles at 15mm needs 300mm of usable bore; 150mm stated gives only 144mm usable (9 tiles). Round 2 additionally ruled out the two escape hatches that don't touch a stated number: (a) the 'waiting grid' beside the column that assemblies/product.py used for rendering is not a legitimate second storage mechanic — idea.json's setup rule requires all 20 stacked physically inside the reserve_column's bore, and the REFILL rule and hero_shot both describe a single continuous readable stack, not a stack-plus-side-tray; (b) no tile orientation or packing trick beats the 15mm pitch without inventing an undescribed tile feature, which the identical-family constraint forbids. Of the two remaining paths — shrinking the 20-tile requirement (which means changing the 12/10/8 star/moon/void split or the 10-well count, both core to the game's stated bust probability and board geometry, i.e. a rules-balance decision, not a dimensional one) versus growing the column to its true required height and tiling the print — growing the column is the fix that touches zero rules numbers (tile counts, well count, win-scoring, and every probability idea.json describes are all unchanged) and uses a print technique (tiling a too-tall part across two prints) this pipeline already supports elsewhere, so it is the smaller-blast-radius change even though the height delta itself (+156mm) is large in absolute terms.

parts.name: plinth_ring
parts.notes: 216mm-diameter, 30mm-tall drum (chamfered skirt) as the base; a central 24mm-diameter axle post rises a further 40mm from the top face, giving a combined standalone bbox height of 30+40=70mm — idea.json states the drum height and the axle rise as two separate numbers and never sums them, so 70mm is my composition, not a stated figure (see unstated_in_spec). OWNS the well diameter (24mm), well depth (6mm), and axle diameter (24mm); every other part's matching feature derives its clearance from these three numbers, never restates them. Ten wells on an 80mm-radius ring at 36deg spacing (index positions 0-9), each with a thumb scallop per blocks.cut_wells' default. Wells at index 0, 4 and 7 additionally carry a 1.2mm raised sunburst collar marking them as zenith wells (feeds the score_rail's raised-slot bonus and the void-in-zenith bust penalty). Rim carries ten 1.2mm index grooves (witness marks for the three discs' notches); top face carries 1.2mm constellation relief continuing across the ring. A residual mechanical detail the builder needs to resolve, not a change to any stated number: the well's 6mm depth puts a seated tile's flat top face flush with the ledge the mask discs rest on, so the tile's 9mm knob rises 3mm past what a single 6mm-thick mask disc can clear locally when un-aligned — cut a shallow (~3mm) relief undercut into the underside of mask_disc_a along the 80mm-radius window-track annulus (outside the through-window openings themselves, which already clear it) so a resting knob never fouls a rotating disc. This does not touch the well diameter, well depth, tile height or axle length — all four stay exactly as stated.

recesses.notes: Representative recess: moon_tile and void_tile share the exact same 22x22x15mm bbox as star_tile (identical outline, thickness, rim and back per idea.json's own load-bearing constraint), so this single recess entry applies identically to all three tile families. Clearance (24-22)/2=1.0mm per side, above the 0.4mm drop-in minimum. Protrusion: a 15mm-tall tile (6mm body + 9mm knob) in a 6mm-deep well sits 9mm proud of the rim, well past the 2mm minimum — the knob is the intended pinch point for 'reach through and pull tiles one at a time'.

parts.name: mask_disc_a
parts.notes: Bottom mask. 216mm-diameter, 6mm-thick disc in the window-track band (11mm-thick outer rim band for stiffness — AMENDED from 9mm to 11mm, see top-level amendments; the extra 2mm gives the underside relief undercut a compliant remaining wall instead of removing the band entirely). 25mm centre bore free-turning on plinth_ring's 24mm axle post — DERIVES its 0.5mm-per-side clearance from the axle diameter the plinth owns, not restated independently. Six 38mm-diameter through windows on the same 80mm-radius/36deg ring plinth_ring's wells use, at index positions 0,1,2,3,4,6 — reuse the identical position list plinth_ring's wells were cut from (see print_plan notes on blocks.py), never a second copy of the trig. Broad rounded paddle grip-tab projects 16mm past the 216mm rim on one side, giving the 232mm x-extent in bbox_mm (216+16); this is a straightforward sum but idea.json never states it as a combined figure, so it is called out in unstated_in_spec. Own witness notch read against plinth_ring's index grooves. Underside carries the 9mm relief undercut along the window-track annulus described in plinth_ring's notes (deepened from the originally-flagged ~3mm once the true worst-case interference — a full 9mm knob, not a partial one — was computed).

parts.name: mask_disc_b
parts.notes: Middle mask. Identical 216mm/6mm(11mm rim, AMENDED from 9mm)/25mm-bore profile to mask_disc_a, stacking directly on it. Same six-window ring, at index positions 0,1,2,3,6,7. Pointed triangular fin grip-tab, 16mm projection (same 232mm bbox x-extent as mask_disc_a), own witness notch. Told apart from mask_disc_a and mask_disc_c by grip-tab silhouette alone, per idea.json's part_vocabulary.

parts.name: mask_disc_c
parts.notes: Top mask. Identical 216mm/6mm(11mm rim, AMENDED from 9mm)/25mm-bore profile, stacking on mask_disc_b. Same six-window ring, at index positions 0,1,3,5,6,8. Notched double-prong grip-tab, 16mm projection (same 232mm bbox x-extent). Idea.json states the three window patterns are chosen so that across all 100 relative rotations the number of fully-aligned wells is never 0 and never more than 4 — a combinatorial property of the three stated index lists, not a dimension, so nothing to translate here beyond carrying the three lists through unchanged.

parts.name: star_tile
parts.notes: 22mm-diameter, 6mm-thick round + a 10mm-diameter, 9mm-tall knurled pinch knob centred on the back, for a total resting height (relief-face down, knob up) of 6+9=15mm — bbox_mm's z. Face carries a 1.2mm raised five-point star. LOAD-BEARING: outline (22mm round), thickness (6mm), rim profile and back (10mm/9mm knurled knob) are IDENTICAL, dimension-for-dimension, to moon_tile and void_tile. The 1.2mm face relief is the ONLY geometry that differs between the three families — no other feature, chamfer, weight, or texture may diverge, since the entire hidden-information mechanic depends on a face-down tile being indistinguishable by feel, sound, weight or silhouette until it is turned face-up.

parts.name: moon_tile
parts.notes: Same 22x22x15mm bbox, same knob, same back as star_tile — see star_tile's notes for the identical-family constraint. Face carries a 1.2mm raised crescent.

parts.name: void_tile
parts.notes: Same 22x22x15mm bbox, same knob, same back as star_tile — see star_tile's notes for the identical-family constraint. Face carries a 1.2mm raised eclipse (a filled disc inside a ring of radial notches). Revealing one busts a turn; a void_tile is never banked into a score_rail.

parts.name: reserve_column
parts.notes: AMENDED (see top-level amendments): 306mm tall, up from 150mm — the true height a 24mm bore needs to hold all 20 reserve tiles (30 total minus 10 seeded into wells) at their physically-forced 15mm knob-up stacking pitch (6mm body + 9mm knob per tile, no nesting possible), plus the same ~6mm top-mouth chamfer allowance the original 150mm figure already budgeted (20*15 + 6 = 306). Flares from a 46mm shaft to a 70mm base; bbox_mm uses the wider 70mm base for both x and y as the conservative bounding footprint (idea.json never states which end is wider, or gives a combined bbox — see unstated_in_spec). 24mm-round bore holds tiles stacked knob-up — DERIVES its 1.0mm-per-side clearance from the 22mm tile diameter plinth_ring's well already establishes, not restated independently. 9mm-wide slot runs the FULL 306mm height down one face, open to the bore: both a visible game-clock (remaining stack height read at a glance, now spanning the true full stack rather than a partial one) and a finger-access channel that reaches the stack at any depth. EXCEEDS the 251mm bed z-limit as a single print — `tiles: 2` — split into two printed segments (a lower ~180mm piece carrying the base taper and a upper ~126mm cap continuing the 46mm shaft, exact split left to the builder) joined by a dovetail/spigot seam aligned so the 24mm tile bore and the 9mm read-slot both run continuously through the joint with no step or ledge a tile or a finger could catch on. Because of the side slot, retrieval here is not the single top-down pinch ergonomics_check's `recesses` formula assumes, so this part deliberately carries no `recesses` block — see the interfaces entry for the reasoning, mirrored from t14's deep-claim floor-chamber precedent.

parts.name: score_rail
parts.notes: 130mm x 30mm x 20mm bar, one per seat (4 players max). Two parallel 6.6mm-wide, 11mm-deep slots stand tiles ON EDGE: a plain front slot and a raised rear slot on a stepped ledge carrying the 1.2mm sunburst-collar motif for zenith winnings. A tile stood on edge presents its 6mm body thickness to the slot width (idea.json's own stated 6.6mm slot minus 6mm tile = 0.3mm clearance per side, under this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum — kept as-is since idea.json states 6.6mm specifically, not approximately; flagged rather than silently widened, see unstated_in_spec) and its 22mm diameter to the slot's 11mm depth (exactly the tile's radius, so a standing tile sits half-buried, 11mm proud — well past the 2mm minimum). No `recesses` block declared here either: standing-on-edge is a different orientation from each tile's primary table-resting bbox (22x22x15, relief-down/knob-up) that the `recesses` formula assumes, so the formula's footprint/depth arithmetic would not describe this pairing correctly. Four end-finials (triangular/square/pentagonal/hexagonal prism cross-section) tell the four rails apart by seat; they sit within the stated 130mm length, not added onto it.

interfaces.notes: Representative for all three tile families (identical bbox). plinth_ring OWNS the 24mm well diameter and 6mm well depth; star_tile/moon_tile/void_tile's 22mm diameter derives its 1.0mm-per-side clearance from that well diameter, not restated independently. Engages the ergonomics_check `recesses` formula directly (matches, since the tile sits flat, relief-down, in its primary table orientation).

Representative for all three tile families. reserve_column's 24mm bore derives its clearance from the same 22mm tile diameter plinth_ring's well interface already uses. Deliberately NOT modelled as a `recesses` block on reserve_column (see that part's notes): retrieval is via the chamfered top mouth for the topmost tile PLUS a 9mm-wide full-height side slot that reaches the stack at any depth, which the flat top-down `recesses` formula does not represent. AMENDED: worst case (last tile, bottom of the true full stack — 20 tiles at 306mm, up from a 150mm shaft that only ever fit 9) is reachable through the side slot at any point along its now-306mm run, not by a straight pinch down the bore; the dovetail seam joining the two printed segments must not obstruct the slot at the join.

Representative for star_tile and moon_tile (the only two families ever banked; void_tile is never placed in a score_rail). Tile stands ON EDGE: its 6mm body thickness fits the 6.6mm slot width (0.3mm/side, tighter than this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum — inherited unchanged from idea.json's own stated 6.6mm figure, not loosened by me; flagged in unstated_in_spec) and its 22mm diameter sinks 11mm into the slot depth (half-buried, 11mm proud). Applies identically to both the plain front slot and the raised rear (zenith) slot — same 6.6mm x 11mm geometry, the rear slot only differs by the 1.2mm sunburst collar marking it. Not modelled as a `recesses` block on score_rail: standing-on-edge is a secondary orientation, not the tile's primary table-resting bbox the formula assumes.

All three mask discs (mask_disc_a/b/c, stacked in that order) share one 25mm centre bore riding plinth_ring's 24mm axle post — the axle diameter is OWNED by plinth_ring; each disc's bore derives its 0.5mm-per-side clearance from it, a loose rotating fit, not restated independently per disc. Engagement depth: 3 discs x 6mm bore-region thickness = 18mm of the axle's stated 40mm length, leaving 22mm of axle exposed above the top disc with no stated retaining cap — idea.json gives no top-cap feature, so none is added (see unstated_in_spec); the stack is held on by gravity and the snug bore fit alone. AMENDED note: the discs' rim-band height grew from 9mm to 11mm (see top-level amendments) but bore engagement depth is measured over the 6mm bore-region thickness only, unchanged — so this 18mm/22mm split is unaffected by the amendment. The full-stack standalone height, separately, grows from 27mm to 33mm; still nowhere near the axle's 40mm length or the bed's 251mm z-limit.

mask_disc_a, mask_disc_b and mask_disc_c stack directly on each other (a then b then c) on plinth_ring's outer rim ledge. Max 3, all sharing the same 216mm-diameter footprint — far too wide (216mm base vs 33mm combined stack height, 11mm each, AMENDED from 9mm/27mm) to topple; the toppling check this interface kind implies is trivially satisfied by the discs' own bulk, not by anything added here.

AMENDED, new interface: reserve_column's two printed segments (306mm total, exceeds the 251mm bed limit as one piece) join via a dovetail/spigot seam. The 24mm tile bore and 9mm read-slot must both run continuous and flush across the joint — no step, ridge or gap large enough to catch a tile edge or a finger. Exact seam geometry (spigot diameter, engagement depth) is a builder decision within the part's own 46-70mm cross-section; not separately dimensioned here since it does not change any other part's interface.

print_plan.notes:
AMENDED: reserve_column (306mm, up from 150mm) now exceeds the 246 x 246 x 251mm bed as a single print and is tiled into two segments (`tiles: 2` on that part) joined by a dovetail/spigot seam — the tallest part in the set by a wide margin (plinth_ring's combined drum+axle is 70mm; the full three-disc stack is 33mm). Every other part still fits the bed in one piece and needs no tiling. plinth_ring prints skirt-down: the ten wells and axle post are both simple vertical features from the flat top face (pockets and a straight upstanding cylinder), no overhangs; the skirt's outward chamfer is within printable overhang angle. mask_disc_a/b/c print flat, rim-down, windows as plain vertical through-holes, grip-tab in-plane — no supports. Tiles print relief-face DOWN against the bed, knob UP — their exact resting/game orientation, not a print-specific one, so the print process itself carries no tell: all three families use the identical bed-contact face (the plain back, minus the 1.2mm relief, which is what's on the bed) and the identical knob-up orientation, meaning nothing about how a tile was printed reveals its family before it's turned face-up. reserve_column's two segments each print standing on their own base, tapering/continuing the 46-70mm profile, self-supporting; the internal bore is an open channel on both segments (the full-height side slot removes any enclosed roof), so no internal supports on either piece, and the dovetail seam prints as a plain in-plane interlock with no overhang of its own. score_rail prints flat on its 130x30 face, slots open upward as plain vertical pockets, finial cross-sections extruded along the bar's length — no supports.

blocks.py notes for the builder: use `cut_wells` directly for plinth_ring's ten wells (it already defaults to a thumb-scallop cutter, matching idea.json's stated scallop). The ten-position, 80mm-radius, 36deg ring that plinth_ring's wells AND all three mask discs' six-window subsets are drawn from must be generated ONCE and reused for all four cuts (plinth wells + 3 disc window rings) plus the plinth's own index grooves and each disc's witness notch, per the shared_positions lesson graduated from turns 14-15 — but note blocks.shared_positions itself is a rectangular cols x rows x pitch grid generator and does not produce a radial ring, so this project needs an equivalent hand-rolled 'generate once, reuse everywhere' radial position list rather than a literal call to that block; do not write the trig four separate times. `seated_pair` is not used for the tile/well fit because idea.json already states both the well diameter (24mm) and the tile diameter (22mm) as fixed numbers, not one derived from the other via a default clearance — recomputing either through seated_pair's free-fit formula (22.8mm) would silently override a stated dimension.

unstated_in_spec: plinth_ring's total standalone height (70mm) is my sum of two numbers idea.json states separately and never combines: a 30mm-tall drum and a 40mm axle rise above it. I did not alter either figure, only added them for the bbox_mm the schema requires.

The vertical relationship between the well floor, the 6mm well depth, and the ledge the mask discs rest on admits more than one reading in idea.json's prose ('the well ring is recessed 6mm below the hub shoulder and the outer rim ledge... so the stack floats clear of the tile knobs'). I read the well's stated 6mm depth as the SAME 6mm step described in that sentence (one recess, not two nested ones), which keeps the recess depth I assert (6mm) strictly traceable to idea.json's own explicit 'six-millimetre-deep' wording rather than inventing a deeper, unstated trough. That reading leaves a real interference between a resting tile's 9mm knob and a single mask disc's window-band material when unaligned. Two build-repair rounds established the true worst case is the FULL 9mm knob (not the ~3mm I originally estimated from a partial-overlap assumption) — the earlier estimate implicitly assumed well_depth buried part of the knob, but well_depth == tile_thickness buries none of it. THIS BRIEF_PROPOSED.JSON amends mask_disc_a/b/c's rim-band height from 9mm to 11mm to give the corrected 9mm-deep relief cut a compliant remaining wall, rather than deepening the well or shrinking the knob (both bigger, less visible changes to the mechanic's numbers).

mask_disc_a/b/c's combined bounding footprint (232mm = 216mm rim + 16mm grip-tab projection) is a direct sum of two numbers idea.json states separately; it is not itself a stated figure, and it is the number that matters for the 246mm bed-fit check.

The 40mm axle post has no stated retaining feature (cap, pin, etc.) once the three discs (18mm of bore engagement) are stacked on it, leaving 22mm of axle exposed and uncapped above the top disc. I did not invent a cap; the stack is held on by gravity and the snug 0.5mm-clearance bore fit alone, matching idea.json's own language ('the disc stack rests on... the ledge') which never mentions a retainer. Unaffected by the rim-height amendment (bore engagement is measured over the 6mm bore region only).

reserve_column's cross-section ('46mm across a 70mm base') reads as a tapered obelisk (70mm foot narrowing to a 46mm shaft) but idea.json never states which end holds which number or gives a single combined footprint; I used the wider 70mm figure for both x and y of bbox_mm as the conservative, structurally-safe bounding box.

RESOLVED by this amendment (was previously flagged unresolved): reserve_column's stacking pitch is physically forced to 15mm per tile (6mm body + 9mm knob, no nesting possible against the tile's stated, load-bearing, identical-across-families geometry). idea.json's original 150mm column height and 20-tile capacity (30 total minus 10 seeded into wells) were mutually incompatible at that pitch — 20 tiles need 300mm, not 150mm — a conflict two independent build-repair rounds confirmed has no geometry-only fix within the original 150mm figure. This amendment raises column_h to 306mm (the true requirement plus the original ~6mm chamfer allowance) rather than shrinking the 20-tile requirement, which would have meant changing idea.json's own 12/10/8 star/moon/void split or its 10-well count — both core to the stated game balance, not dimensional details. The new height exceeds the print bed, so reserve_column is now tiled into two printed segments (see print_plan and the new reserve_column/reserve_column joins interface).

score_rail's slot width (6.6mm, explicitly stated) against a 6mm tile body thickness yields 0.3mm clearance per side, under this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum seat clearance. I kept idea.json's stated 6.6mm rather than widening it, since it reads as a specific, deliberate figure (not a rounded approximation), and flagged the tight tolerance instead of quietly loosening a stated dimension.

score_rail's slot LENGTH (how many tiles a single slot holds side by side, and what per-tile pitch a standing tile's sideways-projecting knob needs beyond the bare 6.6mm width) is not stated anywhere in idea.json, which only gives the rail's overall 130x30x20mm footprint. No rule states a per-rail tile capacity limit, so I did not invent a number for it; left as a builder-level layout detail within the stated 130mm length.

No numeric width/depth is given for the wells' thumb scallop; the well's own clearance (1.0mm/side) already clears ergonomics_check's retrieval formula without it, so I treated the scallop as a stated qualitative feature for the builder to carve via blocks.cut_wells' default rather than asserting a separate scallop dimension of my own.
